The Eye's second half. §bSirius B§r (T5) cools white dwarfs into black ones, and §bthe magnetar§r (T6) runs on Antipolarization Agent. The §bQuasar Engine§r and the first galaxies (T7, T8) follow in a later update.

The bottom rows hold the pack's own UXV parts and machines. The crafted Stargate now waits in §6The Endgame§r, after MAX.
The last voltage tier. Beyond the Stars' part of it comes in a later update: MAX parts built from Eye T9's §bWhite Hole Matter§r, and Eye T10, which makes §bUniversium§r and opens §6The Endgame§r.
After MAX: what Universium is for, the MHDCSM line, and the crafted Stargate.

§6§lGTNH: Beyond the Stars - the Unit One nuclear campus.§r

One controller, one projection, and every inlet cut into the building it feeds. The top two rows are a §bten-step beginner path§r: craft the controller, break ground, project the plant, plumb the points of use, load the rods, first steam, seat the rotors, wire the clock, first EU, read the panel.

The third row is the deep end - laser output, spin doctrine, the propellant and coolant ladders, and the safety sheet. The two fluid ladders open at step 7, one step before the clock, because a chamber with no propellant and no coolant refuses every cycle and the plant never spins. The two middle rows are bills of materials; those do not count toward completion.

§6§lThe bottom row is THE CAMPAIGN§r - and it is where the ten-step path leads. Finishing the build is the beginning, not the end: four milestone lines climb just by running the plant, and the points they pay buy a twenty-five node upgrade tree on the main station controller.

§7Ten steps, in order, and you are making power. You do not need to know anything about this plant to start.§r

§6§lWHAT UNIT ONE IS§r
One nuclear campus raised by ONE hologram projection: a 50x50 platform, a reactor silo fed by falling fuel rods, a 3x3 turbine spine, a 7x7 injection chamber and a rotor gallery. A fully tuned tier-5 plant pushes toward a billion EU/t.

§e§lDO THIS§r
Assemble the §bNuclear Plant Foundation§r in an Assembling Machine (IV, 60s, programmed circuit 4):
  1x Radiation Proof Machine Casing
  4x IV Circuit
  2x Lead Dense Plate
  8x Tungstensteel Plate
  8x Tungsten Rod
  2x Iridium Plate
  2x Rhodium-Plated Palladium Plate
  4 ingots of Molten Platinum

§a§lDONE WHEN§r
The controller is in your inventory. §8Nothing is taken from you - this quest only looks, and once it has seen the controller it stays complete for ever.§r
§8Claim the reward before step 2 plants that controller in the ground.§r

[note]This ONE machine is the whole plant. There are no module controllers any more: the cooling towers, the spine duct, the spiral chamber, the rotor gallery AND the four plant modules (Vent Stack, Switchyard, Extraction Derrick, Enrichment Annex) are all pieces of THIS controller, raised by the same projection.[/note]

§e§lDO THIS§r
§b1.§r Find flat ground with room. The plant is §b50 blocks square§r: the projection measures 32 blocks BEHIND the controller, 17 in FRONT and 25 to each side, and wants 20 to 40 blocks of headroom depending on tier.

§b2.§r Place the Nuclear Plant Foundation. §6Whichever way you are facing when you place it is the plant's FRONT§r - the silo grows straight back from it, and every socket you will ever pipe into faces the way you are facing now.

§b3.§r Open its GUI. Three small unlabelled number fields sit at the bottom right, with a small square §bchart button§r to their left. Reading LEFT to RIGHT:
  §bUpgrade Tree§r - the BUTTON, not a field. Nothing to set yet; it opens the progression tree you will meet at the end of the path. Leave it alone for now.
  §bBuild Tier§r - the NARROW field, 1-5: the silo size the projection raises. §6Start at 1.§r
  §bRPM Limit§r - the WIDEST field, 5 digits: the turbine redline you authorise. Leave it at 12,000.
  §bControl Rods§r - the field on the far right: campaign power, N/24. Leave it at 24.
§8Hover any of the four to confirm which is which. All three fields already hold the value above, so changing nothing here is correct - and putting the tier in the rod field would run the whole campaign at 1/24 power.§r
§8The rod field will accept up to 36 and the RPM Limit up to 19,500, because the milestone lines and the upgrade tree can eventually withdraw the rods past the 24/24 design stop and lift the redline past 12,000. Until they do, anything above those two defaults is clamped straight back to them. Neither ever moves on its own: a tier raises the CEILING, and you type the value you want.§r

§a§lDONE WHEN§r
A §bHologram Projector§r is in your inventory. §8Step 1 paid you one, and nothing is taken from you. That is the whole gate: a quest can only read what you are CARRYING, never what you have built.§r

§e§lCHECK YOUR WORK§r
The controller stands facing the way you want the plant to face, and §bBuild Tier§r is set in its GUI. Neither of those is part of the gate above - but both have to be true before step 3 projects anything, and Build Tier can never be changed once a silo stands.

[warn]Choose the spot properly. Relocating a 50x50 plant later means breaking all of it. And Build Tier only decides what to RAISE: once a silo stands, the projection will never re-tier it - you would have to dismantle the silo first.[/warn]

§e§lDO THIS§r
Right-click the controller with the §bHologram Projector§r. The whole campus appears as a ghost, in this order:

  platform -> silo -> spine duct -> spiral chamber -> rotor gallery + output manifold -> cooling tower, cooling tower -> vent stack -> switchyard -> extraction derrick -> enrichment annex

§aWhat the projection draws is exactly what the structure check wants.§r There is no build-only leniency left anywhere and no second controller to place. In survival the projector pulls blocks straight out of your inventory.

[img height=500]btsquests:textures/gui/plant-overview.png[/img]

§c§lWHAT THE PROJECTOR WILL NOT PLACE FOR YOU§r
It raises walls. It does not fit machines. When it has finished you still have to place, by hand:
  §b12x Turbine Housing§r - 4 in the spine bore, 8 on the gallery centreline. Those cells are left as §cAIR§r,
     §8and they keep showing as ghosts for ever. That is the projector marking the spot, not a job it will finish.§r
  §bevery hatch, injector, sensor and control block§r - those cells come out as §cPLAIN CASING§r. Break the casing, put the real machine in.
  §bthe fuel pillars and rod loading ports§r inside the silo - optional interior, left as air.
Steps 4 to 9 place all of it, and every one of them hands you part of the bill.

§a§lDONE WHEN§r
You are holding the §b64x Light Concrete§r and §b16x Radiation Proof Machine Casing§r listed above. §8Steps 1 and 2 paid you exactly that. Claim this BEFORE you start projecting - in survival the projector eats blocks straight out of your pack as it works.§r

§e§lCHECK YOUR WORK - THE PROJECTION IS FINISHED WHEN§r
Right-clicking the controller with the projector places nothing more. The only cells still empty anywhere on the campus are then the §b12 Turbine Housings§r and the silo interior.

§cThose 12 ghosts never go solid, and you have not done anything wrong.§r The hologram draws them and always will; the survival projector skips them every single time, on purpose, because a housing carries a spin setting and a rotor it has no business guessing. Step 7 places all twelve by hand. Do not stand there clicking at them.

§cThe controller is also still NOT FORMED at the end of this step.§r That is correct too. It is short of its §bMaintenance Hatch§r, its §bFeedwater Input Hatch§r, its §bOutput Hatch§r and its §bDepleted Output Bus§r - four sockets, and they are the whole job of step 4. §6The plant forms at the end of step 4, not here.§r

[note]Only the PLATFORM is mandatory. Silo, spine, spiral, gallery and towers are all optional pieces - but a platform on its own generates nothing, and a silo with no gallery is a steam EXPORT plant rather than a generator.[/note]

§6§lEVERY INLET SITS WHERE IT IS USED§r
There is no plumbing wall. Each insert and extract point is cut into the building it feeds, on the exact course it enters the plant's logic: rods go in at the fuel course they burn on, water at the drum, coolant and propellant at the chamber that spends them, power at the generator.

[img height=480]btsquests:textures/gui/point-of-use.png[/img]

§e§lTHE SILO FACE - the flat wall your controller is set into§r
Three courses, one cell either side of the controller's own column - exactly as drawn above:
  §by2§r  §bROD§r Input Bus . §bDEP§r Depleted Output Bus
     §8the bottom FUEL course - the exact segment the cascade burns§r
  §by1§r  §bH2O§r Input Hatch . §bSILO CONTROL BLOCK§r . §bOUT§r Output Hatch
     §8the drum course - feedwater in, waste water and exported steam out§r
  §by0§r  §bMAINT§r Maintenance Hatch, in the cell beside the main station

§e§lTHE SPIRAL CHAMBER FRONT WALL - one course above the floor§r
  §bCOOL§r Input Hatch - coolant, for the thing that actually overheats
  §bPROP§r Input Hatch - bulk propellant, directly under the eight injectors it stocks
  §bMNT§r Maintenance Hatch - the chamber carries its own, in the floor's front-right corner

§8The output manifold's own sockets - dynamos, energy and lasers - are step 9.§r

§e§lDO THIS§r
Break the plain casing in each socket cell and place the machine there. Then run your logistics to each one; nothing is shared and nothing travels down a pipe you have to build.

§a§lDONE WHEN§r
All §bnine§r machines listed above are in your inventory at the same time.
§8This quest only LOOKS at what you are carrying, and it takes nothing. Hold the whole set at once, CLAIM it, and only then break the casings and set the machines into the wall. Already installed them? Wrench them back out for a moment - the check is on your inventory, not on the building.§r

§e§lCHECK YOUR WORK§r
Right-click the §bSilo Control Block§r you just set into the face. It prints the whole instrument panel, and the REACTOR group carries a §bSupply§r line reading §20 rods queued -> 0 pillar gaps§r.
§8Both zeros are right. A pillar gap is an empty segment in a §bReactor Fuel Pillar Frame§r, and not one of those is standing yet. What this step pays you is §b16 fuel-column BLOCKS§r - one block is one segment and 8 of them make a pillar, so that is §b2 pillars§r - and they go up in step 5. Gaps appear when you raise the pillars; the queue moves when you feed the bus.§r
§6This is the step where the plant FORMS for the first time.§r §8Maintenance, Feedwater Input, Output Hatch and Depleted Output Bus are the only four sockets the structure actually demands, and they all just went in. Everything you fit from here on is added to a plant that is already alive.§r

[note]You never touch a rod port inside the silo again. The controller distributes rods from that one bus to all 45-201 pillars itself, every decay cycle - best grade first, lowest empty segment first.[/note]

§6§lTHE DECAY CASCADE§r
Every fuel pillar is a gravity column 8 segments tall - 8 Reactor Fuel Pillar Frame blocks, stacked. A rod dropped in falls to the lowest empty segment. Only the §bBOTTOM§r one burns; when it is spent it drops into the depleted bus and the stack above shifts down one.

A pillar is §2LIVE§r while its bottom segment holds a burning rod:
  §bsteam = live pillars x 16,384 L/t x fuel multiplier x rods N/24§r

§e§lTHE FUEL LADDER§r
  Uranium §8x1§r   MOX §8x2§r   Thorium-Bonded §8x5§r   Naquadah-Bonded §8x9§r
Same rod, same slot, nine times the steam at the top of the ladder.

§e§lDO THIS§r
Feed fuel rods into the §bRod Input Bus in the silo face§r - bottom fuel course, one cell to the LEFT of the main station §8as you stand outside and look at the silo§r - and keep it stocked. One rod is one segment, about 90 minutes, and a full pillar is roughly 12 hours.

§8You also need the pillars themselves: stacks of Reactor Fuel Pillar Frame blocks, §b8 blocks to a pillar§r, standing inside the silo. The projector treats them as optional interior and leaves those cells empty, so a silo with no pillars makes no steam at all.§r

§a§lDONE WHEN§r
8 Uranium Fuel Rods are in your inventory. §8Claim it, then feed them to the bus - a rod inside the bus is inside a machine, not on you.§r

§e§lCHECK YOUR WORK§r
§6Do the arithmetic before you read the panel, so the number does not surprise you.§r Step 4 paid you §b16 fuel-column BLOCKS§r and 8 blocks make one pillar, so what you are holding is §b2 pillars§r - not 16. Stand them up as 2 stacks of 8, in 2 separate cells of the silo floor.
2 empty pillars are §b16 empty segments§r, so the Supply line reads §20 rods queued -> 16 pillar gaps§r the moment they are up. Drop this step's 8 rods into the bus and it reads §28 rods queued -> 16 pillar gaps§r until the next decay cycle hands them out, then §20 rods queued -> 8 pillar gaps§r.
§cGaps with an EMPTY queue§r is the starving cascade, and that is the reading to act on; §20 gaps§r is a full silo. §8A tier-1 silo has room for 45 pillars - 360 blocks - so 2 is a start, not a finish. Blueprint: Steam Generator has the count for every tier.§r

[warn]Classic fuel ASSEMBLIES in the bus still work, but at HALF output - the panel calls it "Assembly fallback (output halved)". The cascade is where the other half lives.[/warn]

[note]§6Where rods come from changed in 0.24.0.§r The four-step Assembler chain is retired; rods are now built on the §bThe Fuel Line§r row at the bottom of this chapter - twenty-three steps, ore to bundle. §bFour pellets to a rod and three rods to a bundle are unchanged§r, so every rod and assembly you already own is worth exactly what it was.[/note]

§e§lDO THIS§r
§b1.§r Water into the silo face's §bH2O§r Input Hatch - the Input Hatch on the drum course, beside the Silo Control Block. §8Step 4 has the drawn map.§r
§b2.§r Set Control Rods 1-24 in the GUI. 24 is full campaign power. §8A programmed circuit in the controller slot overrides the field.§r
§b3.§r Enable the controller.

With no turbine chain behind it the plant simply §bexports Reactor Steam§r through the silo face's OUT hatch - or Hot Coolant, if you feed it IC2 Coolant instead of water. That is honest power, and it is a fraction of what this plant can do.

§c§lTHE REACTOR NEVER DRAWS EU§r
Nothing on the ten-step path needs to be powered. Unit One generates; it does not consume - the reactor, the spine, the chamber and the gallery draw nothing at all, not idling, not starting, not running - and the four Energy Hatches in step 9 are §bnot a structure requirement§r: this plant forms and runs perfectly well without a single one of them.

§6§lTWO THINGS ON THIS CAMPUS DO DRAW EU. BOTH ARE OPTIONAL MODULES.§r
The §bExtraction Derrick§r (§21,920 EU/t§r) and the §bEnrichment Annex§r (§2480 EU/t§r) take their power §bthrough those same four Energy Hatches§r and from nowhere else. Build either one and the hatches stop being furniture: fit at least one and §bwire it to a live grid§r, or that module silently never turns over. Their blueprints are on the bottom row and both say so at the top.

§e§lREAD IT ANYWHERE§r
The §bSilo Control Block§r prints the same instrument panel the GUI does. So does the Turbine Control Block, and so does a Portable Scanner. §8One panel, everywhere - no readout can disagree with another.§r

§a§lDONE WHEN§r
A §bWater Bucket§r is in your inventory. §8That is the whole gate - a quest reads your pack, not your plant. A bucket PRIMES the feedwater hatch; a reactor that is actually running wants a real water line behind it.§r

§e§lCHECK YOUR WORK§r
The REACTOR group shows live pillars and a non-zero §2L/t steam§r, and OUTPUT reads §2Steam export§r with a real number.

[note]Feedwater is NOT coolant. The hatch you just filled is the SILO's. The Spiral chamber has its own §bCOOL§r hatch, on a different building, and neither can drink the other's fluid. §cStep 8 is where that one has to be fed§r - until it is, the turbine never leaves 0 RPM.[/note]

[warn]Every shutdown leaves DECAY HEAT: twenty minutes of mandatory cooling water. It is deferred, never waived. "Written in Fire" has the details.[/warn]

§6§lTHE END OF THE PIPE§r
Steam leaves the silo down the spine duct, spirals through the injection chamber and blows through the §bROTOR GALLERY§r. Eight stage housings sit on its centreline; four more sit in the spine bore.

§c§lPLACE ALL TWELVE YOURSELF§r
The projector deliberately skips every Turbine Housing cell - it leaves them as §cAIR§r, because a housing carries a spin setting and a rotor it has no business guessing. Craft twelve and place them: §b4§r in the spine bore, filling every other cell starting one block out from the silo, and §b8§r on the gallery centreline, again every other cell. The last of the eight hangs in the manifold mouth.

§e§lDO THIS§r
§b1.§r Right-click each of the eight gallery housings with a §bTurbine Rotor§r. Sneak-right-click empty-handed to pull one back out; the wear stays on the item.
§b2.§r Right-click each of the four §bspine duct§r housings to set its spin - clockwise or anticlockwise. "Spin Doctrine" explains what that buys you; for now set all four the same and move on.

§e§lROTORS WEAR, LIKE REAL BLADES§r
Each stage takes slow random damage at speed - roughly one point per ten minutes at full tilt. Every point costs that stage §c5%§r, and at ten the rotor §cSHATTERS§r. The average factor over all eight sockets multiplies your whole output, so an empty socket is a 12.5% cut.

§6§lTHE PLANT KEEPS RUNNING WHILE YOU DO THIS§r
Placing the eighth gallery housing does not stop the reactor and does not suddenly demand a hatch. It FORMS the Rotor Assembly, and one grey line appears in the OUTPUT group, opening §8Manifold: Energy Hatches 0/4§r and closing §8furniture, not a load; the plant runs without them§r. That is information, not a fault, and step 9 fills those sockets.
§cSkip them for ever only if you never build a plant module.§r The moment an §bExtraction Derrick§r or an §bEnrichment Annex§r stands on this campus, that same line stops saying furniture and starts reading §8the reactor never draws EU; the Derrick and the Annex do, through these§r - and with no hatch fitted at all it turns §cRED§r, because those two draw their EU through these sockets and will not run without one.

§6§lTHE OUTPUT GROUP FLIPS ON THE FIRST ROTOR, NOT ON THE HOUSINGS§r
Twelve housings and no rotors still reads §2Steam export§r, because eight empty seats generate exactly nothing and the plant is genuinely still exporting steam out of the silo. The instant ONE rotor is seated it reads §2Generating§r instead. §8The MATH group re-titles itself on the same instant and for the same reason, so the two can never describe two different plants.§r

§a§lDONE WHEN§r
12 Turbine Housings and 8 Turbine Rotors are in your inventory at the same time. §8Step 6 paid you the twelve housings.§r
§8This step pays four Water Buckets as well as the injectors. They are not for the boiler - they are the first COOLANT for the Spiral chamber, and step 8 will not spin the fan without it.§r
§8This quest only LOOKS at what you are carrying, and it takes nothing. Hold the whole set at once, CLAIM it, and only then break the casings and set the machines into the wall. Already installed them? Wrench them back out for a moment - the check is on your inventory, not on the building.§r

§e§lCHECK YOUR WORK§r
The TURBINE group reads §2Rotors 8/8§r at an average factor near §2x1.00§r, and the STEAM CHAIN group shows §24 housings§r on the spine.

§6§lNOTHING HERE RUNS ON ITS OWN CLOCK - YOU SET THE PACE§r
A §bredstone rising edge§r on the TURBINE CONTROL BLOCK starts one CYCLE. A cycle drinks a buffered 20-tick slug of steam, opens a §b+/-2 tick window§r in which each of the eight injectors fires exactly 1 L of propellant, and adds RPM:

  §bgain = 176 x P x (timed / 8)§r

RPM bleeds off 0.5% every tick and the redline is §b12,000§r. §cNo clock means the RPM decays to nothing, which means no EU at all.§r

§c§lAND A CYCLE IS REFUSED UNLESS THE CHAMBER IS PLUMBED§r
This is the step that catches people. Before a cycle is allowed to start, the plant checks two things about the Spiral chamber: that the injectors have propellant to fire, and that the §bCOOLANT§r hatch can pay for the RPM that cycle would reach. If either answers no the cycle is §cREFUSED§r - no steam drunk, no propellant burned, no heat added, and §bno RPM§r.

§cSo a clock wired to a dry chamber leaves the whole plant at 0 EU/t for ever.§r It does not blow up and it does not break; it simply never spins, and the panel prints the reason on a §bHOLD:§r line. Both fluids go into the chamber's FRONT WALL, one course above the floor - §bCOOL§r at one end, §bPROP§r at the other. Step 4 put those two hatches in. §6This step is where you fill them.§r

§a§lCLAIM THIS QUEST BEFORE YOU FIT ANY OF IT§r
Every machine named below goes INTO the plant, and this quest only reads what you are CARRYING. Hold the §bTurbine Control Block§r, the §bSpine Sensor§r and all §beight§r Precision Injectors at once, claim it, and only then start breaking casings. §8Already fitted some? Wrench them back out for a moment - the check is on your inventory, not on the building.§r

§c§lFIT THE EIGHT INJECTORS FIRST§r
The spiral chamber has eight §bPrecision Injector§r sockets, one per interior level - world y 3 up to y 10 - each in the middle of one wall, walking round all four walls as the helix descends. The projector leaves every one of them as plain Tungstensteel Turbine Casing: break the casing and put the injector in its place.
§8Two of them stand 7 and 8 blocks above the platform. Bring scaffolding or fly.§r
The §bSpine Sensor§r goes in the chamber ROOF, front-centre, facing UP.

§e§lTHEN DO THIS, IN THIS ORDER§r
§b1.§r Set the Turbine Control Block into the §boutput manifold back face§r - centre column - and put the manifold's own §bMaintenance Hatch§r into the socket directly below it. Step 9 has the map.
§b2.§r §6COOLANT into the chamber's §bCOOL§r hatch.§r §bPlain water counts§r - it is the bottom rung of the ladder, and a fan at a few hundred RPM drinks tens of litres a tick, not thousands. Empty your four buckets into it, then run a real water line in behind them. "The Coolant Ladder" is open now and has the rest.
§b3.§r §6PROPELLANT into the chamber's §bPROP§r hatch§r, at the other end of the same wall. §bBenzene§r is the honest first rung (§2P x1.25§r). The line stocks all eight injector reserves and the plant lands the timed shot for you. "The Propellant Ladder" is open now too.
§b4.§r §bOnly then§r run a redstone clock into the Turbine Control Block. About §bone pulse per second§r is the sustainable rate, because that is how fast one slug of steam is produced.

§8How many injectors count as TIMED is simply how many the line kept stocked when the edge arrived - a line that only keeps 5 of 8 runs at 5/8 gain. Hand injection still works, and still has to hit the window.§r

§a§lDONE WHEN§r
The Turbine Control Block, the Spine Sensor and all §bEIGHT§r Precision Injectors are in your inventory together. §8Steps 4 and 7 paid you four injectors each - that is the eight, and they are the eight this step installs. All of it has to be on you AT ONCE: four now and four later counts as zero.§r
§8This quest only LOOKS at what you are carrying, and it takes nothing. Hold the whole set at once, CLAIM it, and only then break the casings and set the machines into the wall. Already installed them? Wrench them back out for a moment - the check is on your inventory, not on the building.§r
§8The four Water Buckets step 7 paid you are deliberately NOT part of this gate. You pour them away into the COOL hatch here and an emptied bucket is a different item, so a gate that asked for them could never be met by anyone who followed the instructions. Fill the hatch whenever you like; the quest cannot see it either way.§r

§e§lCHECK YOUR WORK§r
The STEAM CHAIN group reads §2Spiral 8/8 injectors§r and its coolant line has stopped saying §cCoolant NOT SUPPLIED§r - it now names the fluid with a live L/t figure. The TURBINE group shows a rising §2RPM§r and a §2cyc/min§r figure, and the §bSpine Sensor§r pulses once per ACCEPTED cycle. Use that pulse as your confirmation.
§8Nothing in this step stops the plant either - the reactor runs straight through it.§r

[note]Pulsing faster than steam is produced misses cycles - and a missed cycle still burns the eight litres the line had stocked. If the panel prints a §bHOLD:§r line, read it: it names the exact hatch or the exact reason. The two that stop a NEW plant dead are §cinjectors are dry§r and §ccoolant cannot cover§r, and each of them names the hatch to fill and says the cycle was refused rather than run badly.[/note]

§6§lWHERE THE POWER LEAVES§r
The output manifold BACK FACE, and nothing else. Nothing is ever built behind it at any tier, so every socket on it looks out at open sky - three courses of four, plus the control column.

[img height=400]btsquests:textures/gui/manifold-face.png[/img]

§e§lDO THIS§r
Put four §bDynamo Hatches (IV)§r into the four D sockets and run cable off them. Put four §bEnergy Hatches (IV)§r into the four E sockets one course above.

  §bEU/t = L/t x spine speed x efficiency x (RPM / 500) x average rotor factor§r

§6§lWHY ENERGY HATCHES ON A GENERATOR§r
§bThey are never a STRUCTURE demand.§r The reactor, the spine, the chamber and the gallery consume nothing - no draw, no idle cost, no start-up cost - so leaving all four E sockets empty can never un-form the plant or stop the campaign, and while any are missing the OUTPUT group prints one grey line counting them.

§c§lTHEY ARE NOT FURNITURE, THOUGH. TWO MODULES RUN ON THEM.§r
Two of the optional modules on the bottom row draw their power through these four sockets and from nowhere else:
  §bExtraction Derrick§r §21,920 EU/t§r while it drills
  §bEnrichment Annex§r §2480 EU/t§r while it enriches
§cBuild either one with no Energy Hatch fitted - or with one fitted and nothing wired into it - and that module silently never turns over.§r So fit at least one §bEnergy Hatch (IV)§r here and run a live cable INTO it: your base grid, or straight off one of the Dynamo Hatches in the row below. Both modules running at once is §22,400 EU/t§r, which a single IV hatch carries on its own.
§8The panel backs this up: with a module standing and no hatch, that grey line turns RED and names the Derrick and the Annex.§r

§cThe DYNAMOS are the ones that matter.§r Until a Dynamo or a Laser Source sits in that face, everything the turbine makes is thrown away - and the panel says so in as many words: §6Weakest term:§r §2output ceiling 0 (0%)§r §8- fit Dynamo or Laser Source Hatches in the manifold's back face - nothing can leave§r.

§c§lTHE TRAP§r
Output is clamped to the SUMMED capacity of the dynamo row and the laser row. Four IV dynamos alone are §c32,768 EU/t§r - on a tier-5 build that is 0.003% of what the plant is actually making, and the rest is simply thrown away. The panel prints §cCLAMPED from§r when that is happening, and "Break the Clamp" fixes it.

§a§lDONE WHEN§r
Four Dynamo Hatches (IV) and four Energy Hatches (IV) are in your inventory together. §8Step 8 paid you the four Energy Hatches.§r
§8This quest only LOOKS at what you are carrying, and it takes nothing. Hold the whole set at once, CLAIM it, and only then break the casings and set the machines into the wall. Already installed them? Wrench them back out for a moment - the check is on your inventory, not on the building.§r

§e§lCHECK YOUR WORK§r
The OUTPUT group reads §2Generating§r with EU/t leaving, your cables are live, and the grey Energy Hatch line has gone.

[warn]A multiblock handed more EU than its hatches can take DETONATES in GregTech. The controller clamps before it emits, which is exactly why an undersized output row costs you output instead of your base.[/warn]

§6§lTHE PLANT SHOWS ITS WORKING§r
At the foot of the GUI - and of both control blocks, and the scanner - sits a group called §bMATH§r: §8how that EU/t is derived§r. It walks your CURRENT output in four numbered steps, every factor carrying the value it has right now:

§e§lHOW EACH ONE IS FED - AND HOW IT CANNOT BE CHEATED§r
§bUPTIME§r counts only ticks on which the plant actually put EU on the grid. An idle plant sitting in a loaded chunk earns nothing, and no amount of engineering makes it count faster: 72,000 ticks is one hour, every hour. It is the shallowest ladder on purpose - the line that just wants you to keep the lights on.
§bBURNUP§r scores one segment per live pillar per cascade cycle, §6weighted by rod grade§r. 201 uranium pillars score 201. The same 201 pillars on Naquadah-Bonded rods score §b1,809§r. A bus-fallback slice runs at half output and scores at half rate. This is the line that says §8your fuel chain is not finished§r - and it is why this quest asks for the top rod.
§bREPROCESSING§r scores on the DEPOSIT, never on the tick: one per Extraction Derrick load, one per Enrichment Annex batch. A load parked waiting on a full bus scores once, when it lands. It is the only line that needs a BUILDING, so its rewards go straight back into those two modules - and the only line that speeds ITSELF up.
§bTURBINE§r needs the steam slug §6AND§r all eight injectors landed inside their window. A fast clock with no fuel scores nothing - no slug, no credit. Seven of eight timed scores nothing at all. The chain refills one slug every 20 ticks, so §63,600 perfect cycles an hour is the ceiling and nothing raises it§r - the buffer unlocks raise the burst, never the fill rate. Its ladder is sized against exactly that number: tier 7 is about 333 hours of cycling, which seats it between REPROCESSING (~208 h) and BURNUP (~497 h).

§e§lTHE SHAPE OF IT§r
One free root - §bUnit One Commissioning§r, 0 points - and four branches hanging off it, §6one per milestone line§r, six nodes deep:

  §bUPTIME§r branch        water, steam buffer, baseload output
  §bBURNUP§r branch        rod seals, recladding, deeper burns, more rods withdrawn
  §bREPROCESSING§r branch  solvent recovery, an extra centrifuge stage, module automation
  §bTURBINE§r branch       rotor balancing, bearings, nozzles, overspeed certification

A node needs the node above it on the same branch, and §6a node at depth N on a branch needs THAT branch's milestone line at tier N§r. One rule, no table: the branch that rewards your turbine is the branch the TURBINE line opens.

The four deepest nodes also each need a depth-4 node from the NEXT branch round, so the end of the tree forces breadth. You cannot rush one branch to the bottom and ignore the other three.

§e§lBUYING AND REFUNDING§r
§bLeft-click§r a node to buy it. §bRight-click§r to refund it. The button's own tooltip says so: §8Left-click a node to buy it, right-click to refund. Refunds are free, unlimited, and refused only when another node you hold hangs off it.§r

§aRefunds cost nothing and there is no limit on them.§r Every point goes back the moment you hand a node back, so the tree is somewhere to experiment rather than a decision you regret for the rest of the campaign. The one refusal is the obvious one: you cannot refund a node that something you still hold is hanging off. Refund the far end of the branch first.

Hover any node for its full story - title, effect, cost, what it needs, which milestone tier opens it, and §6exactly which one requirement is currently failing§r. There is no second window to open.

§e§lWHAT THE NODES ACTUALLY DO§r
A node moves one of twelve numbers, and only those twelve: plant output, the control-rod cap, feedwater condensate stages, the steam buffer, cycle RPM gain, the turbine redline, rotor life, Derrick and Annex cycle speed, Annex batch size, the Derrick's tantalum interval, heat rejection, and the decay-heat window. Every one of them starts at a value that does nothing, and every node only ever moves it in your favour.

Bought in full the tree is worth §2x1.450§r on plant output on top of the milestone term, §2+6§r on the control-rod cap, §2x1.30§r on the redline with §2x1.40§r on the cycle gain to reach it, §2x1.75§r on rotor life and §2x1.50§r on both process modules.

§6The tree pays for itself in the right order.§r The rod nodes push the control-rod cap past 24/24, which raises steam - and therefore feedwater. The same tree's condensate nodes cut that feedwater draw by two more halvings. The water branch pays for the fuel branch.

- Tick §bAuto§r in the GUI's Hole control panel: a Seed in a bolt bus then opens a closed hole, and a Collapser closes an open one, with no button.
- BHC Utility Hatches on the cage give redstone while the hole is open. Invert it into an export bus holding Seeds, and a hole that evaporates reseeds itself.

§a§lDONE WHEN§r you hold 64 Neutronium bolts (HOLD → CLAIM → INSTALL).

As the materials around you achieve transcendental properties, pistons and gases stop being enough. The answer is gravity: a black hole, held in a cage of mirrors and coils and spun fast enough that its ergosphere can be put to work.

The §bKerr Ergosphere Engine§r (KEE) holds the hole and does nothing else: it runs no recipes. The machines that use the hole are the §bKerr modules§r, separate machines standing in the cage's arcs (next quests).

§e§lMAKE IT§r The controller is an §bAssembly Line§r recipe: scan a §bBlack Hole Seed§r in the Scanner to research it. NEI shows the rest.

§e§lBUILD§r
- Hologram Projector, stack 1: Kerr T1, 76 × 65 × 71. Chunk-load all of it.
- The Black Hole Compressor's own Extreme Density Space-Bending Casing, Hawking Radiation Realignment Focus and Naquadah Alloy frames, plus our Superradiant Mirrors, Mirror Backing, Ergosphere Field Coils, Beam Focusing Quadrupoles, Beam Dumps, Harmonic Lining and 232 Bolt Injector Rails. The optional task is the full bill.
- Hatches: 1 laser or up to 2 energy hatches in the governor arc, 1 to 8 §bbolt buses§r (plain input buses) on the cage, and optional BHC Utility Hatches beside them. No maintenance hatch.
- Hologram markers 7 and 8 show where the two module controllers go.

§e§lRUN§r Everything is in the GUI.
1. Put a §bBlack Hole Seed§r in a bolt bus and press Open: the hole opens at §b8 SM§r (solar masses).
2. It bleeds mass as Hawking radiation, §b3.2 / M² SM a tick§r. Small holes die fast.
3. The §bgovernor§r fires bolts from the bolt buses to hold your §bsetpoint§r (2-64 SM at T1):
- Neutronium 1/64 SM, Cosmic Neutronium 1/32, Infinity 1/16, Transcendent Metal 1/8, SpaceTime 1/4 SM a bolt;
- at most 4 / 8 / 16 bolts a tick with Mk I / II / III rails. The §llowest§r rail sets the rate, so upgrade them all together.
4. While open, the hole draws §b8,388,608 EU/t (1 A UEV)§r of containment. Without power the governor stops; below 2 SM the hole evaporates. The power switch does §lnot§r stop the hole.
5. A §bBlack Hole Collapser§r in a bolt bus closes it safely: press Collapse twice.

[note]Mass sets the modules' bonus: a bigger hole gives more parallels, a smaller one more speed. The controller tooltip has the full block list, and NEI's Multiblock tab previews both tiers.[/note]

§a§lDONE WHEN§r you hold the controller (HOLD → CLAIM → INSTALL: claim before you place it).

[note]The Black Hole Compressor quest is left as the pack wrote it, because pack edits are turned off (questbookPackEdits in config/beyondthestars.cfg).[/note]

So you have made yourself an Eternal DTPF or hopefully a few, and now it is time for the push onwards.

Beyond the Stars replaces TecTech's Eye of Harmony with §bone Eye that grows from T1 to T10§r, a band at a time, with a §blive star§r at its centre. A star is not a batch recipe: it burns every minute, it must be fed, and it must be held steady.

§e§lBUILD§r
- Hologram stack 1 is the T1 core, 102 × 52 × 80. Chunk-load the whole footprint.
- It is mostly TecTech's own Eye blocks: 9,390 Reinforced Spatial and 4,704 Reinforced Temporal Structure Casings (the Condensate Assembler makes these 32 at a time here), Infinite SpaceTime Energy Boundary Casing, Quantum Glass and the three field generator families.
- On the plinth: gas input hatches for Hydrogen and Helium, an input bus for Stellar Ignition Charges, an ME Output Bus, an ME Output Hatch and a maintenance hatch.
- Power is §bwireless EU only§r, and none of it comes back: the Eye makes matter, not power.

§e§lLIGHT IT§r Put §bStar Chart: Sol§r in the controller slot (never consumed). Sol lights when:
- a §bStellar Ignition Charge§r is in a plinth input bus;
- the buffers hold §b600,000,000 L each of Hydrogen and Helium§r: 10 cycles of upkeep (kept) plus the 100,000,000 L seed cloud (burned);
- the wireless network holds 10 cycles of EU, which the ignition spends.
The protostar contracts for about 40 seconds, then lights.

§e§lRUN§r Every §b60 s cycle§r Sol burns §b50,000,000 L Hydrogen + 50,000,000 L Helium§r and §b1.51 × 10¹¹ EU§r (about 1 A UMV), and makes §b50,000 L Raw Stellar Plasma§r (Raw Star Matter in the GUI) into the ME output hatch. Upkeep is paid in full in every zone; a bad zone only cuts the yield.

§e§lAUTOMATE§r Inputs drain into internal buffers every second, so ME stocking input hatches on the gas sockets work. Keep a few charges in the plinth bus from an ME Interface. A dimension display block in the slot runs planets instead (see §cPlanets on the Eye§r).

[warn]§lSpacetime Compression gates the tier.§r An Eye of tier N needs every compression generator at tier N or higher. Crude runs T1.[/warn]

[note]The next quests teach the stability field, planets and the road to T2. The controller tooltip and GUI carry every number.[/note]

§a§lDONE WHEN§r you hold the controller, Star Chart: Sol and an Ignition Charge (HOLD → CLAIM → INSTALL).

[note]The pack's own Eye of Harmony quest is left as the pack wrote it, because pack edits are turned off (questbookPackEdits in config/beyondthestars.cfg).[/note]

A live star is not a recipe. Every second the Eye updates a §bstability field§r. At T1 it has one gauge, §bP§r (pressure balance): minus is collapse, plus is expansion, and §b0 is the target§r. Each higher star adds a gauge.

§e§lZONES§r The worst gauge sets the zone, the yield and Integrity:
- §bResonant§r within ±10: yield ×1.25, Integrity +1 a second
- §aStable§r within ±40: ×1.00, +0.2
- §eStrained§r within ±70: ×0.50, −0.5
- §cCritical§r within ±100: no yield, −2
- §4Breach§r beyond ±100: the star is lost at once
§bIntegrity§r (0-100) at 0 also loses the star. A lost star costs the star and its unfinished cycle, §lnever§r blocks, cores or unlocked tiers. Relight it with a new charge.

§e§lTRIM§r Pour trim fluids into the §bField sockets§r: 8 plain input hatches on the core band. They are never buffered, and ME stocking hatches there are refused. At T1, 1,000 L Helium is §bP −2§r and 1,000 L Hydrogen is §bP +2§r, up to 10 units a second.

§e§lSENSE§r A §bStellar Field Sensor Hatch§r (8 sockets on the core band) reads one channel against a threshold and emits redstone on all sides: digital (15 above or below the threshold) or analog (0-15 across the range). Channels: P, Θ, Ω, Π, the Agent shield, Integrity, Stability, zone, event warning (+, − or any) and upkeep OK. Right-click it to set it up.

§e§lAUTOMATE§r The standard rig:
- a sensor on §bP > +10§r → a Fluid Regulator cover, or an ME fluid export bus with a redstone card → Helium into a Field hatch;
- a second sensor on §bP < −10§r → Hydrogen.
Covers on the sensor's own side work, wireless redstone transmitters included, so one sensor can drive a valve anywhere.

[note]Sol settles at about P +35 (Stable) by itself, so T1 runs unattended; the rig earns the ×1.25. Higher stars do §lnot§r settle. A binary Directive Hatch and OpenComputers support are coming in a later update.[/note]

§a§lDONE WHEN§r you hold a sensor hatch. Here is a second one for the rig.

Planets are still §bbatch runs§r, as TecTech ran them. They give TecTech's ores and plasmas, but §lno§r Raw Stellar Plasma or dwarf matter: those come only from stars now.
- Put the planet's dimension display block in the controller slot.
- By Eye tier: §bT1§r rocket tiers 0-3, §bT2§r 4-6, §bT3§r 7-8, §bT4§r the Deep Dark.
- A tier N Eye runs every planet of tiers 1..N, at §b×2 parallel per tier above§r the planet's.
- Each compression tier above the planet's TecTech tier takes 3 % off the time.
- EU comes from wireless when a run starts.

[warn]One target per Eye: selecting a planet puts your star out. A second Eye for planets keeps the star burning.[/warn]

[note]One Deep Dark run on the same Eye is a T4 → T5 milestone.[/note]

§a§lDONE WHEN§r you tick the box: this one is information only.

Hold §bResonant for 600 seconds in a row§r and the Eye locks in: §byield ×1.5§r until the streak breaks. The GUI's field line counts it as §lLock n/600§r.

Every milestone's Resonant time counts §lreal§r seconds, so the time dial cannot shortcut it. A tidy rig is how you climb: tighter sensor thresholds (around ±5) keep a star inside ±10 more of the time.

§a§lDONE WHEN§r your Eye's GUI shows Lock at 600/600 or more and Y 1.50; then tick the box (a state is not an item).

Kerr T2 is the same KEE, made denser. Right-click the controller with the §bKerr Density Upgrade§r: it is consumed, permanent, and survives a wrench.

§e§lBUILD§r The cage then needs the T2 reinforcement (hologram stack 2, 92 × 65 × 89): 8,316 Bastion Plates, 677 Casimir Plates, more Harmonic Lining and more glass. The optional task is exactly the difference. A T2 Kerr with the reinforcement torn down will §lnot form§r.

§e§lWHAT YOU GET§r
- setpoints up to §b512 SM§r, so more module parallels (⌊√M⌋ is 22 at 512 SM, against 8 at 64 SM);
- §bKerr Densification§r on the Compressor Module, with a hole of §bat least 128 SM§r.

§e§lMAKE IT§r In the Condensate Assembler (NEI: Condensate Assembling). The big costs are §b4,000,000 L Entangled Raw Star Matter§r (Raw Stellar Plasma, condensed 1 : 1; NEI: Condensate Entanglement) and §b32 Black Hole Seeds§r, so your T1 Eye pays for it. NEI has the whole recipe.

[note]Growing a hole to 512 SM takes a lot of bolts: SpaceTime bolts (1/4 SM each) and Mk III rails do it fastest.[/note]

§a§lDONE WHEN§r you hold the upgrade (HOLD → CLAIM → INSTALL).

Sirius A is a hotter, younger star, and it pushes back. Every tier unlocks in order, in the same three steps:
1. §bmilestones§r on the current star;
2. §bthe core§r, right-clicked into escrow;
3. §bthe transition§r, a live event you have to survive.

§e§lMILESTONES§r On Sol: §b20,000,000 L Raw Stellar Plasma§r made and §b2 h Resonant§r (real time). The GUI and scanner count them, and they stay with the controller through a wrench.

§e§lCORE§r Right-click the controller with the §bStellar Mass Core§r (Condensate Assembling, 256,000 L Entangled Raw Star Matter). It is consumed §lonly§r when the transition succeeds. Sneak-punch with an empty hand to take it back.

§e§lMASS INFUSION§r Build the §bbeam band§r (hologram stack 2: 2,856 Beam Band Casing) and bring compression to tier 2. Buffer §b5,000,000 L Raw Stellar Plasma§r plus Sirius A's first cycle, then put §bStar Chart: Sirius A§r in the slot while Sol burns. For 10 minutes the plasma pours into Sol and P is pushed §b+4 a second§r, so your rig must hold. Survive it and Sol becomes Sirius A, with T2 unlocked for good. Fail and you lose Sol and the plasma, never the core.

§e§lRUN§r Each cycle: §b12,500,000 L Hydrogen + 12,500,000 L Helium + 25,000 L Raw Stellar Plasma§r and 6.04 × 10¹¹ EU (about 1 A UXV), for §b2,500 L Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture§r. A relight takes a charge and a 200,000,000 L seed of each gas.

§e§lTRIMS§r As Sol (Helium P −2, Hydrogen P +2 per 1,000 L), now up to 20 units a second. The beam band's 6 stellar sockets take input hatches for the star's fluids.

[warn]Sirius A drifts P +2 a second and breaches if left alone: run the rig. Helium leaves §lash§r, −0.5 % yield per 1,000 L dosed that second, so a two-stage rig (small doses near 0, big ones far out) beats full-blast valves.[/warn]

[note]A higher Eye still hosts lower stars, at ×2 parallel per tier above. There is one live star per Eye.[/note]

§a§lDONE WHEN§r you have held the core and the chart before the core goes into escrow (that task latches), and then 1,000 L of Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture, Sirius A's first product.

Arcturus is a red giant: a helium core inside a hydrogen shell. It brings a second gauge, §bΘ (core heat)§r, which runs away on its own, and P now climbs with Θ.

§e§lUNLOCK§r
- Milestones on Sirius A: §b1,000,000 L Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture§r and §b3 h Resonant§r.
- The §bShell-Burning Core§r in escrow (Condensate Assembling, 128,000 L Entangled Excited Stellar Plasma).
- The §bjet crescent§r built (stack 3: 2,750 Jet Crescent Casing; the beam band must stand too) and compression at tier 3.
- §b250,000 L Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture§r buffered, plus Arcturus's first cycle.
Then swap in §bStar Chart: Arcturus§r.

§e§lSHELL IGNITION§r (10 min) Θ appears at 0 and ramps in. The T3 trims below, Super Coolant included, work from the start. It ends in one §bforced helium flash§r at 600 s, warned at 585 s: pre-cool and ride it.

§e§lRUN§r Each cycle: §b12,500,000 L Hydrogen + 12,500,000 L Helium + 1,250 L Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture§r and 2.42 × 10¹² EU (about 1 A MAX), for §b625 L Raw Hyperdense Stellar Plasma§r.

§e§lTRIMS§r Up to 20 units a second each:
- Helium (1,000 L): P −1, Θ +3;
- Hydrogen (1,000 L): P +3, Θ +0.5;
- Super Coolant (100 L): P −1, Θ −3.
To pull P down without heating the core, dose Helium §land§r coolant together. Add a sensor pair on Θ driving the coolant.

§e§lHELIUM FLASHES§r Every 20-40 minutes a flash adds §bΘ +30 a second for 3 s§r. The sensor's event channel warns §b15 s ahead§r: pre-cool on the warning and you stay Stable.

[note]The T3 → T4 milestones: §l400,000 L Raw Hyperdense Stellar Plasma§r, §l4 h Resonant§r, and §l3 flashes ridden§r (never worse than Stable from the warning until 30 s after).[/note]

§a§lDONE WHEN§r you have held the core and the chart before the core goes into escrow (that task latches), and then 1,000 L of Raw Hyperdense Stellar Plasma.

Fast-forward a red giant into a §bneutron star§r, and stop it going supernova. The Core Collapse is the hardest event yet: read all of this before you start.

§e§lBEFORE§r
- the T3 milestones;
- the §bGalactic Upgrade Core§r in escrow (Condensate Assembling, 32,000 L Entangled Hyperdense Stellar Mixture);
- the §bspiral arms§r built (stack 4: 5,325 Galactic Shell Plating) and compression at tier 4;
- Arcturus lit and Stable;
- buffered: §b5,000 L HSM§r (the seed), up to §b90,000 L molten SpaceTime§r (the shock absorber) and the neutron star's first cycle;
- §b94,000 L Tachyon Rich Temporal Fluid§r on hand for the Field sockets.
Then swap in §bStar Chart: Neutron Star§r.

§e§l1 FAST-FORWARD§r (about 16 min) Dose Tachyon Rich Temporal Fluid into the Field sockets, up to 100 L/s. The core climbs from 0.50 to §b1.44 M☉§r over 94,000 L. The envelope swells P and Θ as it goes, and your T3 rig must hold.

§e§l2 BOUNCE§r The HSM becomes the neutron seed, Integrity drops 20, and a shock of §b+150§r hits P and Θ.
- Every §b1,000 L molten SpaceTime§r buffered cancels 1 point, up to 90: the shock is then +60.
- Any gauge above +100 after the shock is §c§lSUPERNOVA§r: Arcturus, the Time fluid, the HSM and the SpaceTime are lost. The core stays in escrow.
So bring P and Θ §lbelow +40§r before the bounce. The scanner predicts both.

§e§l3 SETTLE§r The neutron star lights at P 0, Θ +60, Ω +30. Get it Stable for 60 seconds in a row within 180 s (Super Coolant pulls Θ down). T4 is then yours.

§e§lTHE NEUTRON STAR§r
- No fusion, so no Hydrogen or Helium: §b144 L molten SpaceTime§r a cycle and 9.66 × 10¹² EU (about 4 A MAX) hold it.
- Set the §bHSM feed§r in the GUI (0-1.5 L/s, default 0.694). §bWhite Dwarf Matter = 3.6864 L per L of HSM fed§r, about 9,200 L an hour at the default.
- The feed pushes P, Θ and the spin §bΩ§r up. Ω runs away by itself, and §bglitches§r kick it +20 every 15-30 minutes §lwithout warning§r.
- Trims, up to 10 units a second: Spatially Enlarged Fluid (100 L) P −2; molten SpaceTime (100 L) P +2; Super Coolant (100 L) Θ −3; molten Purified Tengam (36 L, up to 5) Θ +1, Ω −4.
- If it breaches, it collapses into a black hole. With T4 unlocked, a dark Eye holding the Neutron Star chart relights Arcturus from a charge and reruns the Core Collapse by itself, with no core. Keep the Time fluid, HSM and SpaceTime stocked for it.

[note]The Deep Dark planet runs at T4, and one Deep Dark run is a T4 → T5 milestone.[/note]

§a§lDONE WHEN§r you hold the core and the chart (HOLD → CLAIM → INSTALL: claim before the core goes into escrow).

A mega mixer: a glass mixing column wrapped in a shear helix, inside a spiral volute with three feed vessels. It turns §bRaw Stellar Plasma into Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture at 100 : 1§r, with no gases, no ignition and no stability field to watch.

§e§lBUILD§r
- Project it from the controller at the tip of the volute's discharge throat (hologram stack 1 = T1, 69 × 70 × 73).
- A fluid Input Hatch on top of each Feed Vessel (3 at T1), an Output Hatch on the throat, and an Energy or Laser Hatch on the bottom cap rim. No maintenance hatch.

§e§lRUN§r §b100,000 L Raw Stellar Plasma → 1,000 L Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture§r in 240 s at UMV: 1 parallel, no overclock.

Turns stockpiled Raw Stellar Plasma into Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture unattended: no hydrogen, helium, ignition or field. It costs 100 L per 1 L, 10× the Raw Stellar Plasma an Eye T2 needs, so it suits banking a Sol surplus or a hands-off line, not replacing Sirius A.

§e§lAUTOMATE§r Plain GT: ME input hatches on the vessels, an ME output hatch on the throat.

[note]It does §lnot§r skip T2: Eye T2 is still required, and only an Eye hosting Sol makes Raw Stellar Plasma.[/note]

§a§lDONE WHEN§r you hold the Homogeny controller and 1,000 L of Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture.

§bTime Dilation§r generators above the star's tier open the §btime dial m§r: a speed-up for the whole star.
- The cap is §b1 + 0.25 × (lowest Time Dilation tier − star tier)§r, at most ×3.00.
- Each +0.25 costs §b10 × 2^(N−1) L/s of Tachyon Rich Temporal Fluid§r (N = the star's tier), drawn from the Field sockets. Paid short, the dial runs slower.
- m speeds up everything the star does (upkeep, product, EU, drift, noise and events) but §lnot§r your trims. A faster star is harder to hold.

§bStabilisation§r generators calm the star: noise and event size × (1 − 0.05 × (lowest tier − 1)), down to ×0.60 at tier 9.

Set the dial with the GUI's − / + buttons (right-click: four steps). It is held at ×1 during transitions, and milestone Resonant time counts real seconds, not dial seconds.

§a§lDONE WHEN§r you hold 1,000 L of Tachyon Rich Temporal Fluid.

A white dwarf, §bcooled into a black dwarf§r. Sirius B burns nothing and has no upkeep: it runs in §bbatches§r, and your job is to follow a cooling curve.

§e§lUNLOCK§r The T4 milestones: §b147,456 L White Dwarf Matter§r from cycles never worse than Stable, §b4 h Resonant§r, and §bone Deep Dark run§r on this Eye. Then:
- put the §bSubspace Cooling Core§r in escrow;
- build the §bsecond arms§r (stack 5: 5,065 Galactic Shell Plating) and bring compression to tier 5;
- put §bStar Chart: Sirius B§r in the slot. The neutron star goes out: one star per Eye.
§bFirst Cooling§r is your first batch. A mean yield of at least 0.9 with no fracture unlocks T5; fall short and the core stays for another try. The batch's Black Dwarf Matter comes out either way.

§e§lBATCHES§r Each batch takes §b18,432 L White Dwarf Matter§r and assembles a white dwarf at Θ +90. Over §b2 h§r (÷ the dial) the cooling setpoint ramps from §b+90 to −90§r; at T5 the Θ gauge reads your error from that setpoint. Output: §b4,608 L Black Dwarf Matter × the batch's mean yield§r. EU: 3.87 × 10¹³ a cycle (about 16 A MAX).

§e§lSUBSPACE COOLING§r Trims:
- Dimensionally Shifted Superfluid (100 L, up to 10 a second): Θ −1, P −0.5. The heat sink.
- Raw Stellar Plasma (1,000 L, up to 5): Θ +3, for an overshoot.
- Helium (1,000 L, up to 10): P +2, accretion pressure.
Decay heat pushes Θ up the whole way and crystallisation drags P down. Expect about §b100,000 L of Superfluid a batch§r.

§e§lTHE PLATEAU§r While the setpoint crosses −10..+10 (about 800 s), latent heat adds §bΘ +0.15 a second§r. The event channel warns 15 s ahead.

§e§lAUTOMATE§r Θ reads the error from the curve, so one sensor pair on Θ drives the Superfluid valve all batch long; a pair on P drives Helium. Keep White Dwarf Matter stocked for the next charge.

[warn]§lFracture§r (Breach or Integrity 0) ends the batch at 25 % of its output × the fraction done.[/warn]

[note]One T4 Eye on the default feed makes about enough White Dwarf Matter for one T5 Eye.[/note]

§a§lDONE WHEN§r you hold the core and the chart (HOLD → CLAIM → INSTALL: claim before the core goes into escrow).

SGR 1806-20 is a §bmagnetar§r, the most magnetic object known. White and black dwarf matter merge into it, and its field has to be untwisted for as long as it lives.

§e§lUNLOCK§r The T5 milestone: §b6 batches§r at mean yield 0.9 or better with no fracture. Then:
- put the §bMagnetar Seed Core§r in escrow;
- build the §bgalactic rim§r (stack 6: 7,286 Galactic Shell Plating) and bring compression to tier 6, with §bno star lit§r;
- buffer the merger charge: §b18,432 L White Dwarf Matter + 4,608 L Black Dwarf Matter + 100,000 L Antipolarization Agent§r;
- put §bStar Chart: SGR 1806-20§r in the slot.

§e§lMAGNETAR MERGER§r The dynamo winds the polarity §bΠ§r up by itself (+0.5 a second); no flares yet. Agent doses pull Π back toward 0.
1. §bImprint:§r hold Π inside +60..+90 for 120 s in a row, within 600 s.
2. §bRelease:§r bring Π back inside ±40 within 60 s.
A failure spends the charge and keeps the core.

§e§lRUN§r Each cycle: §b3,000 L Antipolarization Agent§r (the constant feed) and 1.55 × 10¹⁴ EU (about 64 A MAX), for §b15 L Magnetar Matter§r.
- The merger charge also fills a 60-cycle §bdwarf-matter reserve§r. At 10 cycles left the Eye tops it up from the buffers with §b1,800 L White Dwarf + 450 L Black Dwarf Matter§r; an empty reserve starves the magnetar. Keep both stocked.
- The Eye gives back §b12 Purified Tengam dust per 1,000 L§r of Agent burned, through the ME output bus.

§e§lTHE FIELD§r Four gauges: P, Θ, Ω and Π, and Π runs away by itself.
- The Agent feed charges the §bflare shield A§r (it settles near 40 with no trim). The shield soaks up to 25 Π a second.
- §bGiant flares§r come every 60-120 s, warned §b15 s ahead with their sign§r, and push Π ±25 a second for 4 s.
- Pre-charge the shield on the warning: Agent in a Field socket, 100 L = A +4 (Θ +0.5), up to 5 a second.
- The other trims are the neutron star's: Spatially Enlarged Fluid, molten SpaceTime, Super Coolant and molten Purified Tengam.
Lose the magnetar and a re-merge needs the charge again, but not the core.

[note]Magnetar Matter is the planned upkeep of Eye T7 and a base of the T9 pellets, both coming in a later update.[/note]

§a§lDONE WHEN§r you have held the core and the chart before the core goes into escrow (that task latches), and then 1,000 L of Magnetar Matter.

The Homogeny's second tier: a middle stirring ring, three more feed vessels and the outer spokes around the same controller. It mixes at §b4 parallels§r and adds §bDegenerate Stellar Mixture§r: 72 L molten White Dwarf Matter + 72 L molten Black Dwarf Matter + 1,000 L Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture → 1,000 L in 60 s.

§e§lUPGRADE§r (permanent)
- Build the stirring ring: hologram stack 2. Each new vessel takes a fluid Input Hatch on top.
- Mix §b100,000 L§r of Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture in this Homogeny.
- Right-click the §bHomogeny Tier II Core§r (Condensate Assembling) onto the controller. Sneak-punch with an empty hand returns it.
- Press Install in the GUI, or use a screwdriver: §b10 minutes offline§r at UXV power. A mix already running finishes first. Progress shows in the GUI and the scanner, and survives a wrench.

Degenerate Stellar Mixture feeds the Homogeny T3, the Eternity Shell Casing and the Reality machines (Tier 14 - MAX). Three Galactic Shell cells on the stirring ring's outer face are reserved for Quasar ports, later.

[note]The Tier II Core is built from §btwice as many UMV parts§r (32 Field Generators, 64 Electric Pumps) for now: the pack's UXV Field Generator and Pump still need Universium, which only Eye T10 makes. UXV circuits are fine (the Polychrome or Dimensional Quantum Circuit).[/note]

§a§lDONE WHEN§r you hold a Homogeny Tier II Core and 1,000 L of Degenerate Stellar Mixture (claim before you install the core).

Tengam with its electrons swapped for positrons is literally §bantipolarised§r. Field-cooling it locks the reversed domains, and its counter-currents untwist a magnetar's field.

§e§lCHAIN§r
1. Raw Tengam → Electromagnetic Separator → Purified Tengam → Polarizer → §bAttuned Tengam dust§r.
2. §bLarge Chemical Reactor§r (UXV, 20 s): 16 Attuned Tengam dust + 100 L Semi-Stable Antimatter + 144 L molten SpaceTime → §b1,000 L Positronic Tengam Slurry§r.
3. §bVacuum Freezer§r (UXV, 10 s): 1,000 L slurry + 2,000 L Super Coolant → §b1,000 L Antipolarization Agent§r.
Semi-Stable Antimatter comes from the Antimatter Forge (SSASS).

§e§lUSE§r
- the magnetar's §bconstant feed§r, 3,000 L a cycle (50 L/s);
- the Magnetar Merger charge, 100,000 L;
